cases.prompt: Our OrderService has @Transactional and an EntityManager, and the Order class is annotated with @Entity and jpa persistence imports. We want to test our pricing rules fast. Where should each of these go?
expectations: States that Order must lose @Entity and move to a persistence adapter class named as a row model, with an explicit mapper between row and domain
States that jakarta.persistence and org.springframework imports are forbidden in the domain package
Moves @Transactional to the use case entry point and removes it from domain and adapter methods
Declares a plain OrderRepository port in the domain and makes the existing Spring Data interface the implementation
Recommends setting spring.jpa.open-in-view to false and adding an ArchUnit test that fails on outward imports

cases.prompt: We are a team of 4 building an internal admin CRUD app over 6 tables. No business rules beyond required-field validation. A colleague says we should do full Clean Architecture with domain, application and adapter rings plus ports. Should we?
expectations: Recommends against full rings for this case and gives the reason that there is no invariant to protect
Proposes the lowest structure that pays: adapter.in.web plus a service, validation in the request record, no domain ring and no ports
Identifies a specific trigger that would justify adding rings later, such as a non-trivial pricing or eligibility rule
Names one concrete thing to add now, for example open-in-view false plus a projection for lists
Does not propose a rewrite of the existing service layout

cases.prompt: Our OrderController has an if statement checking status before cancel, then calls orderRepository.save(order). Review the layering of this service and tell me what to change.
expectations: Identifies business branching in the controller and an entity passed straight to the repository from the transport layer
Moves the status check into a domain method on the aggregate that throws a named domain exception
Introduces an application service as the single transaction entry point that loads, mutates, and saves
Returns a record or void from the controller rather than the managed entity
Explains that an entity escaping the transaction causes lazy loading during serialization

cases.prompt: PlaceOrderUseCase builds a query string with EntityManager to find orders for a customer since a date. We want to keep JPA out of the use case but we also do not want to write a repository interface for every query. What is the pragmatic approach?
expectations: States that no query mechanism of any kind belongs in the use case, including plain interfaces
Proposes one intent method on the port such as findByCustomer with a domain-level parameter type
Implements that method in the persistence adapter with Specification, a JPQL query, or a derived query
Rejects interface-per-use-case as noise and explains the port should describe a collaborator, not a use case
Confirms the use case unit test then needs no EntityManager and no Spring context

cases.prompt: We have 400 files in a flat layout: controllers, services, entities, repositories all under com.acme.shop. We cannot do a rewrite before our Q3 release. Give us a plan that does not fork the architecture effort.
expectations: Rejects a rewrite and proposes an incremental slice-by-slice sequence
Puts the cheapest highest-value steps first, namely moving controllers and request records, then setting open-in-view false
Requires characterisation tests to be added before any code moves
Orders the steps so each is independently shippable and revertible, ending with flipping an ArchUnit rule from log to failure
Advises picking one vertical slice such as one endpoint and doing not start with the most-called code

cases.prompt: We added @ComponentScan for domain, application, adapter and vendor so the beans all register. Now the domain package gets a repository injected and we cannot tell which layer is which at runtime. How do we make the rings real?
expectations: Explains that component scanning draws no boundaries and rings exist only as package convention plus a test
Removes the wide @ComponentScan and keeps the bootstrap class at the package root with default scanning
Narrows scanning to explicit @Import of adapters and points @EntityScan and @EnableJpaRepositories at the adapter package
Adds an ArchUnit test asserting the domain package has no framework dependencies and application does not depend on adapter
States that use cases must depend on ports rather than on adapter classes for the boundary to hold at runtime
